lines.text: Stanley sold $73M a year. Then one cup went viral.
Not a new cup. Stanley, the old flask maker, already sold this one, and it barely sold.
So who saw it first? Three women who ran a shopping blog. They bought a batch themselves, sold it to their readers, and it was gone in days.
So what changed? Stanley hired a new boss from Crocs. He found the blog, and sold the cup to women, in new colours.
Sales jumped to $94M, climbed to $194M, and hit $402M.
And Stanley added scarcity: limited colour drops. Shops put up signs limiting how many cups you could buy.
Four years later, Stanley was projected to sell more than $750M in a single year.
Spot one in a cup holder today, and remember: it once barely sold.

Beat 'boss': 'Stanley took the hint, and hired a new boss from Crocs' states Stanley hired Terence Reilly because of The Buy Guide's success. The source (CNBC, 23 Dec 2023) does not say that: Reilly joined in 2020 as president (seven years at Crocs) and learned of the blog on a listening tour after he arrived. Unsourced motive/causation about a real company. Fix e.g.: 'So what changed? Stanley hired a new boss from Crocs. He found the blog, and sold the cup to women, in new colours.' (lower third 'Stanley's new president, from Crocs' is also more exact than 'boss').

Beat 'turn': 'And the trick was scarcity' plus the overlay 'Scarcity / the real product' presents scarcity as THE cause. CNBC credits women buyers, 100+ colours and social media, with Reilly wanting only 'a little bit of scarcity' in limited-edition drops; the video's own CTA asks 'scarcity or the colours'. Conclusion beyond the source. Fix e.g.: 'And Stanley added scarcity: limited colour drops. Shops put up signs limiting how many cups you could buy.' and drop 'the real product' (e.g. sub 'limited drops'). The limit-signs claim itself is confirmed (CNBC: Target stores limited two per person; Reilly's quote).
